llm.summary: The ApiFlash skill is mostly a coherent connector, but its setup instructions tell users or agents to run unverified remote installer scripts directly in a shell.

dimensions.detail: The declared tool scope is Bash(oo *), which is proportionate for connector use; the documented installer commands exceed that normal operating scope.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: First-time setup includes curl-to-bash and PowerShell irm-to-iex installer commands without version pinning, checksum/signature verification, or explicit approval before running them after an oo command-not-found failure.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger language is broad for any ApiFlash request, but the runtime flow is otherwise schema-first and connector-scoped.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill does not ship persistence or background workers, but the unverified remote installer can install persistent local tooling or alter the user environment outside the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Normal operation is scoped to ApiFlash through the OOMOL oo connector, with listed actions for screenshot capture, quota lookup, and screenshot metadata.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill carefully before installing. Routine ApiFlash actions appear scoped to the oo connector, but do not run the documented remote installer commands unless you trust OOMOL's installer source and are comfortable with local code execution; prefer a verified or package-manager installation path where available.
llm.findings:
[SC2] unexpected: The artifact does contain a direct remote shell installer for the oo CLI; installing a helper CLI is related to setup, but this execution pattern is not necessary or sufficiently bounded for ordinary ApiFlash connector use.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad ApiFlash activation language matches a service connector pattern, but it would be better scoped to explicit ApiFlash actions to avoid incidental activation.
[T03] unexpected: The static finding is supported by the macOS/Linux and Windows setup snippets that execute remotely fetched scripts; this supports Review, not malicious intent, because the behavior is disclosed and setup-related.
